newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Peru sign pact to boost joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: India, Peru sign pact to boost joint ventures.

text.p: India and Peru signed an agreement on Tuesday to set up a joint business council to promote contacts between private firms of the two countries.

Visiting Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori witnessed the signing of the agreement by A.S. Kasliwal, president of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), and Juan Forsyth, director-general of Peru's Crosland Tecnica S.A.

"Basically, it (the agreement) is to exchange delegations and assist in trying to find business partners and sources of information," Vijay Topa, a senior FICCI official, told Reuters after the signing ceremony.
Topa said the council would help in the formation of joint ventures and lead to regular exchanges of business visitors, in coordination with government trade committees.
Trade fairs highlighting business opportunities were also possible, he said.

Fujimori arrived on Sunday for a four-day visit aimed at raising the profile of his Latin American nation in India and attracting investment. He met Indian leaders on Monday, and officials signed six cooperation agreements.
Fujimori was scheduled to visit industrial plants and meet business leaders in the financial centre of Bombay and its industrial satellite town, Pune, on Wednesday.

Two-way trade is fairly small at this stage. In 1996, India exported goods worth $41 million to Peru, mainly motorcycles, bicycles, tyres and tubes, three-wheel vehicles, pharmaceuticals and automobile and bicycle parts.
India's imports, mainly fishmeal, zinc and pima cotton, totalled $15 million.
